value: The PTSD vs HC whole brain VBM analysis revealed significant differences in GM volume in bilateral amygdala, hippocampus, putamen, parahippocampal gyrus, and left thalamus, with the PTSD group showing reduced GM compared to controls.

The PTSD group showed significant GM reductions across frontal regions including bilateral cingulate gyrus anterior division, frontal medial cortex, frontal orbital cortex, frontal pole, middle frontal gyrus, and paracingulate gyrus, as well as bilateral insula and precuneus cortex.
These findings suggest widespread grey matter reductions in frontal and subcortical regions in PTSD compared with healthy controls.

value: Significant grey matter reductions in the PTSD group when compared with TC were present across cortical and subcortical regions, including bilateral posterior cingulate gyrus, hippocampus, and frontal medial cortex.
The left frontal pole and right thalamus also presented larger volumes of reduction in PTSD compared with TC.

The PTSD vs TC findings provide evidence of grey matter reductions in PTSD relative to trauma-exposed controls, while some regions showed reductions to a lesser degree than in the PTSD vs HC analysis.

description.value: Two T1-weighted MP-RAGE images per subject were averaged with FSL to improve signal-to-noise ratio. FSL-VBM preprocessing included brain extraction, nonlinear standard-space transformation, intensity inhomogeneity correction, FAST4 grey-matter segmentation, affine and nonlinear MNI registration, creation of a study-specific template, modulation for Jacobian warping, visual quality inspection, and Gaussian smoothing with a 7.06 mm FWHM kernel.
